Further, it has been my experience that the same companies with the same fundamentals can trade at two vastly different prices/valuations depending upon whether the market in general is in a "risk on" or a "risk off" mode. Prior to April 9th, you got a sense of what "risk off" looks like. At the moment, I think it is fair to say the stance is much more "risk on." 
 
When the market has experienced the type of dramatic shift we have seen since April, I think it may be wise to consider the risk/reward ratio of the market's current state. That is, how much upside is left here if things go well and how much downside is there if something causes the market to move back to a "risk off" mode? 
 
For me, I have had an absolutely amazing run since the tariff pause as I took an extremely aggressive stance given I felt the line of least resistance in the markets was clearly higher at that point. And now, I feel as though that line of least resistance may have shifted a bit. If that is correct, what is a swing trader like me supposed to do? 
 
PLEASE NOTE I AM NOT SAYING MY ASSESSMENT IS CORRECT AND THE MARKET CAN CONTINUE RIPPING FOR SOME TIME. However, I play the long game and I am always trying to put the odds in my favor. So...what have I done? Personally, I have taken SOME profits on a number of stocks that have made amazing runs these past three months. I still hold positions in those stocks but my overall stance is definitely less aggressive. 
 
Why might I do that? Again, I am playing the percentages. If the stocks continue to go higher, I still have positions and can benefit. I mean...who know how high these stocks can go, right? However, many of the stocks in my portfolio felt to me as though they are in the higher end of their ranges (consistent with a "risk on" market) and I see the upside as not having the amount of room to move higher as it did on April 9th with the tariff pause.  
 
On the other hand, if something shifts the market into a "risk off" mode (I can think of a number of possibilities where that can happen), I don't want to get caught flat-footed and lose the vast majority of the extraordinary gains I have accrued over the past three months. As I have said before, I believe in the Wall Street adage that 'Bulls and Bears make money and Pigs get slaughtered.' 
 
Once again, can I be wrong and the markets rip another 30% higher from here? Of course. However, I simply and playing the odds and I don't see that as a high probability. If they do continue to rip higher, I still benefit (just not as much). Conversely, if something causes a shift in market sentiment, much of my profits have been secured. I also watch the markets every day and will continue to trade based on what the market is telling me. However, if the market does correct quickly, I am not interested in having the conversation of "Why didn't I take profits when the market was so strong?" 
 
Please note this is simply the way I approach the market to continue to play the probabilities and allow me to win over time. I am not interested in trying to achieve overnight riches. If quick riches is someone's goal then I would say feel free to disregard all of the above.

I wanted to follow-up on the re-shared post below. Specifically, I wanted to elaborate more on the following paragraph where I wrote: 
 
"If you trade for a living like I do, I wanted to make this post to encourage everyone to develop a system to help you consistently make money. I am not saying you can’t make money at times without a system. However, my experience is that there are a lot of “Boom/Bust” retail traders out there. That is, these traders take big risks that pay off when the market is in a “Risk On” mode. But, these same traders have never learned the discipline professional traders use so they often lose most (if not all) of their gains when the market shifts its posture. That is, their portfolios ‘Boom’ when the markets are ‘Risk on’ and ‘Bust’ when the markets are ‘Risk off.’ My goal is to not lose gains and consistently make money regardless of what the market does. " 
 
In regards to these ideas of 'Boom/Bust' and 'Risk On' and 'Risk Off,' there was an interesting Wall Street Journal article from yesterday entitled:  
 
"Why Are Stocks Up? Nobody Knows" 
 
- A torrent of bad news hasn’t been enough to sink the market 
 
Here is a link to the article: 
 
https://www.wsj.com/finance/stocks/why-are-stocks-up-nobody-knows-e40e5f42?gaa_at=eafs&gaa_n=ASWzDAiHH-1ghRl8PkoLOxl98JvxYUNuiX-Y6rA_SHNAQnPnr77fQj-IuP8_oUZg3S4%3D&gaa_ts=68811b94&gaa_sig=2WLHpcS_v_CKeHg1HrWvnVV7SF3i3Lx8l3DcIfQvJIi4ctQRZdvJ-EGsgRTUmcO9lyheCNEhQ7DCSdcT_SQoiQ%3D%3D 
 
In line with the article above, I have to say that it seems like everything is working right now. Why just today I had five stocks in my portfolio achieve double digit percentage gains today alone (btw, consistent with my investing strategy, I took some profit on all of them). 
 
Now...to be clear, I am riding this wave right now just like everyone else. In fact, there is an industry saying that: 
 
‘Everyone is a genius in a bull market.’  
 
IMHO, when the market gives us the opportunity, we do need to be aggressive and take advantage of it. I am no different than anyone else. 
 
However, I have also been around long enough to know that the type of roaring move higher we have experienced since April 9th isn't going to go on forever. For example, at some point, fundamentals will matter again and stocks (and crypto) without earnings or any inherent value aren't going to be pumped through the stratosphere by the rampant speculation of animal spirits running wild.  
 
When the exuberance dies down (and, IMO it will at some point), that is when we will find out which investors have a plan and a system to protect themselves when things turn. Those that have learned the discipline that successful traders use will be prepared while those who have reinforced risky habits of speculation will get hurt. It is just the way things have always worked. 
 
As Warren Buffet once said: 
 
'Only when the tide goes out do you discover who's been swimming naked.' 
 
I would encourage everyone to have a plan in place for when the tide does go out. I don't know when that will happen but the probability of it happening at some point seems to be increasing. Of course, I have no idea what the market is going to do nor do I try to tell it what to do. However, I have created a system for myself for the times when the market is not going up non-stop like it has been recently.  
 
My only question to anyone reading this post is...  
 
'Do you have a system in place to protect yourself if/when the market pulls back?'  
 
If not, you may want to consider implementing one. 
 
I wish everyone nothing but the best.
